t.5.18.1: With sweet and expressive words, Rāvaṇa made his intent known to her, the forlorn, joyless and pitiable lady who sat surrounded.
t.5.18.3: I desire you, O wide-eyed one; hold me in high regard, my beloved, O you who are endowed with excellence in every limb, O enchanter of the hearts of all the worlds.
t.5.18.2: Seeing me, you whose thighs are like an elephant's trunk, you hide your breasts and belly, and out of fear you wish, as it were, to make yourself invisible.
t.5.18.4: There are no men here, nor any rākṣasas who change their form at will. Let your fear that has arisen on my account depart, O Sītā.
t.5.18.5: O timid one, it is in every way the very own dharma of the rākṣasas, there is no doubt of this, either to go to the wives of others or to carry them off by force.
t.5.18.6: Thus it is, Maithilī: I will not touch you while you are unwilling, though desire may indeed course through my body as it pleases.
t.5.18.7: O lady, there is no cause for fear here; trust in me, my beloved. Show me your love in truth, and do not be thus absorbed in grief.
t.5.18.8: A single braid, the bare earth for a bed, brooding thought, a soiled garment, and fasting even when there is no occasion for it: these things are not fitting for you.
t.5.18.10: Precious drinks, carriages and couches, song, dance and instrumental music, all these you shall obtain, O Maithilī, by attaining me.
t.5.18.9: Variegated garlands, sandalwood and aloewood, and garments of many kinds, as well as celestial ornaments.
t.5.18.11: You are a jewel among women; do not be like this. Put ornaments on your limbs. Having won me, how could you, O lovely-bodied one, remain unworthy of them?
t.5.18.12: This beautifully blossomed youth of yours is passing away; what has gone by does not return again, like the swift current of the waters.
t.5.18.13: I think that the Maker of the universe, the creator of beauty, ceased from his work once he had made you, for there is indeed no other woman equal to you in beauty, O lovely one.
t.5.18.14: O Vaidehī, having come upon you, endowed with beauty and youth, what man could pass you by, even were he the Grandsire himself?
t.5.18.15: O you whose face is like the cool-rayed moon, whatever limb of yours I look upon, O broad-hipped one, on that very limb my eye becomes fastened.
t.5.18.16: Become my wife, O Maithilī; cast off this delusion. Among my many excellent women, be my chief queen.
t.5.18.17: The jewels that I have seized from the worlds, having ravaged them, all of those, O timid one, along with this kingdom and I myself, are yours.
t.5.18.18: Having conquered the whole earth, garlanded with many cities, I will give it to Janaka for your sake, O playful lady.
t.5.18.19: I see no other in this world who could be a match for me. Behold my exceedingly great valor, unrivaled in battle.
t.5.18.20: Time and again in battle the suras and asuras have been routed by me, their banners crushed; they are unable to stand in the ranks arrayed against me.
t.5.18.21: Desire me; let the finest adornment be done for you today, and let radiant ornaments be fastened upon your body. I would see your beauty, well joined with adornment.
t.5.18.23: Sport freely with me, trusting me, and command me boldly; and while you delight yourself through my power, let your kinsmen too live in delight.
t.5.18.22: Adorned with your toilette and full of graciousness, O fair-faced one, enjoy pleasures as you desire; drink, O timid one, and take your delight. Give away as you please, whether land or riches.
t.5.18.24: Behold my prosperity, my splendour and my fame, good lady; what will you do with Rāma, who is clad in bark garments, O fortunate one?
t.5.18.25: Rāma, who has cast aside victory, whose fortune is gone, who roams the forest, bound by vows and sleeping on the bare ground, I doubt whether he is alive or not.
t.5.18.26: O Vaidehī, Rāma will not even be able to catch sight of you, like moonlight veiled in front by dark clouds accompanied by cranes.
t.5.18.27: Nor can Rāghava win you back from my hand, any more than Hiraṇyakaśipu could win the glory that had passed into Indra's hand.
t.5.18.28: O lady of charming smile, of lovely teeth, of beautiful eyes, O playful one, O timid one, you carry away my mind as Suparṇa carries off a serpent.
t.5.18.29: Having seen her, slender, clad in soiled silk, and though unadorned, I find no delight in my own wives.
t.5.18.30: However many women I have dwelling in my inner apartments, endowed with every virtue, O Jānakī, exercise sovereignty over them all.
t.5.18.31: O lady with dark-black tresses, the foremost women of the three worlds are mine indeed; they shall wait upon you as the Apsarases wait upon Śrī.
t.5.18.32: O lovely-browed one, whatever jewels and riches there are with Vaiśravaṇa, enjoy them, and the worlds, and me as well, O fair-hipped lady, just as you please.
t.5.18.33: O lady, Rāma is not equal to me in austerity, nor in strength, nor in feats of valour, nor in wealth, nor even in splendour or in fame.
t.5.18.34: Drink, roam about, take delight, and enjoy pleasures; I bestow upon you heaps of wealth and the earth as well. Sport with me as you please, O lovely woman, and let your kinsmen too, gathering around you, make merry.
t.5.18.35: O timid one, your limbs adorned with spotless golden necklaces, roam with me through the forests born on the shores of the ocean, thick with clusters of blossoming trees and filled with bees.
